# FORGE reference (generated by tools/gen_docs.py — do not edit)

## Ops (63; 33 with GPU kernels)

Every op has a float64 scalar reference that each lowering is tested against.

| op | class | inputs | shape rule | tolerance | fusion | attrs | GPU | semantics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `matmul` | contraction | 2 | matmul | rel:1e-4 | epilogue |  |  | batched a[..., m, k] @ b[k, n] or b[..., k, n] |
| `matmul_t` | contraction | 2 | matmul_t | rel:1e-4 | epilogue |  | yes | a[..., m, k] @ b[n, k]^T (weight layout of HF linear layers) |
| `attention` | contraction | 3 | attention | abs:1e-5 | no | causal,groups,scale,window | yes | naive scaled-dot-product attention; q[s,hq,d] k[t,hk,d] v[t,hk,d] -> [s,hq,d]; GQA via groups |
| `moe_ffn` | contraction | 5 | same | rel:1e-4 | no | k,norm,scale,gating |  | sparse MoE SwiGLU FFN: h[t,d], router logits[t,e], gate/up[e,f,d], down[e,d,f]; per token top-k experts (ties -> lower index; gating 0 softmax, 1 sigmoid), weights renormalised over the k if norm, times scale; y = sum_k w * down_e(silu(gate_e h) * up_e h) |
| `add` | elementwise | 2 | broadcast | exact | yes |  | yes | y = a + b (numpy broadcasting) |
| `sub` | elementwise | 2 | broadcast | exact | yes |  | yes | y = a - b |
| `mul` | elementwise | 2 | broadcast | exact | yes |  | yes | y = a * b |
| `div` | elementwise | 2 | broadcast | ulp:1 | yes |  | yes | y = a / b |

| `minimum` | elementwise | 2 | broadcast | exact | yes |  | yes | y = min(a, b) |
| `pow` | elementwise | 2 | broadcast | rel:1e-5 | yes |  |  | y = a ^ b |
| `fma` | elementwise | 3 | broadcast | exact | yes |  |  | y = a * b + c (single rounding) |
| `select` | elementwise | 3 | broadcast | exact | yes |  |  | y = c != 0 ? a : b  (inputs: a, b, cond) |
| `neg` | elementwise | 1 | same | exact | yes |  | yes | y = -x |
| `abs` | elementwise | 1 | same | exact | yes |  | yes | y = /x/ |
| `sqrt` | elementwise | 1 | same | ulp:1 | yes |  | yes | y = sqrt(x) |
| `rsqrt` | elementwise | 1 | same | rel:1e-6 | yes |  | yes | y = 1 / sqrt(x) |
